domain: SEC filing-clock aggregate fundamentals: balance-sheet expansion velocity of the sector filer panel, aggregated point-in-time through the canonical bridge (research/assets/stocks/pit_conditioning.py); PIT-conditioned proposal (contributes to the >=3-of-6 quota; no price-derived conditioning claim)
title: Aggregate balance-sheet expansion velocity as a priced negative signal for sector ETFs: long contracting sector filer panels, short expanding ones, market-neutral, on the frozen 12-ETF cohort
mechanism_question: Does the rate of change (year-over-year expansion/contraction velocity) of the point-in-time aggregate balance sheet of a sector's SEC filer panel predict the forward after-cost return of the corresponding sector ETF relative to a risk-matched SPY context? Concretely: is a sector whose panel-wide equal-weight mean of us-gaap:Assets is contracting (or expanding slowly) a BUY versus a sector whose aggregate balance sheet is expanding rapidly, once SPY/sector beta is removed and after 10 bps/side costs? The mechanism is deliberately a FLOW (velocity of the asset base), not a LEVEL (its size) and not any price-derived quantity.
falsifiable_prediction: Directional and specific, preregistered with no sign rescue: the cross-sectional relation between aggregate asset growth g_i(t) = ln(M_i(t)/M_i(t-252 sessions)) and forward sector-ETF excess returns is NEGATIVE (q-theory / overinvestment direction). Operationally, the anchor book (long the 3 lowest-growth eligible sectors, short the 3 highest-growth, hysteresis 3+3, +/-1/6 per leg, quarterly 63-session clock, net ~ 0) must show, over S0 2018-04-04..2025-07-31 with 3 frozen folds: (i) after-cost expectancy > 0 at 10 bps/side; (ii) position PF >= 1.10; (iii) at least 2/3 folds positive; (iv) MDD <= 15%; (v) positive incremental alpha versus the frozen risk-matched SPY context overall AND risk-matched excess positive in at least 2/3 folds; (vi) the asset-LEVEL control must NOT reproduce the result under its preregistered rule (|control incremental alpha| < 0.5 x |anchor incremental alpha| and control expectancy <= 0), and a control that outperforms a negative anchor falsifies the family outright (V2/V4 lesson, L6). If the realized sign is opposite (expanders outperform), the anchor loses and the family is rejected as specified - the opposite-sign reading (q-theory reverse / growth-premium) is a different family and is not proposed.
literature: Zhang, L. (2005), 'The Value Premium', Journal of Finance 60(1): 67-103 - investment-based (q-theory) asset pricing: high-investment firms have structurally lower expected returns because their cost of capital is low; investment is the primitive negative predictor of the cross-section.

Cooper, M., Gulen, H. and Schill, M. (2008), 'Asset Growth and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns', Journal of Finance 63(4): 1609-1651 - firms with high total asset growth earn abnormally lower subsequent returns; the effect is read as overinvestment/agency and discount-rate dynamics of the expanding balance sheet. This is the exact single-name anomaly whose sector-aggregate transmission the anchor tests.

Titman, S., Wei, K.C.J. and Xie, F. (2004), 'Capital Investments and Stock Returns', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 39(4): 677-700 - increases in capital investment predict significantly negative abnormal returns, consistent with managers overinvesting free cash flow at the expense of shareholders.

Lyandres, E., Sun, L. and Zhang, L. (2008), 'The New Issues Puzzle: Testing the Investment-Based Explanation', Review of Financial Studies 21(6): 2825-2855 - investment and financing effects share one investment-based channel; used here only to justify why the REAL-side flow (assets) and the FINANCING-side liquidity state (A4-H2's cash family) are separable mechanisms with distinct testable objects.

pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.canonical_bridge: research/assets/stocks/pit_conditioning.py ONLY: conditioning_panel(records, filer_sectors, sessions, field, max_filing_gap_days) over the frozen SEC instant-fact store (3,817,158 records, 410-filer panel, store sha256 f53eb3712bc9d686ec8a91b3715beaf73be1e5243a89af1816bd62eea51df955). No other aggregation path is authorized; no fundamental quantity is derived from OHLCV (plan 6.P2 no-proxy rule).
fields_used_pit: us-gaap:Assets - sole conditioning field of this family. Coverage census (packet, pre-S0 availability fraction, floor 0.80): XLB 0.975, XLC 0.85, XLE 0.80, XLF 0.90, XLI 1.00, XLK 0.90, XLP 1.00, XLRE 1.00, XLU 1.00, XLV 0.925, XLY 0.975 - FUNDABLE in all 11 sectors; the full sector cohort is rank-eligible on data grounds.
pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.fields_not_used_pit: all other SEC fields (shares outstanding, public float, cash, current assets, equity, long-term debt - the last is census-fundable in only 2/11 sectors and is rejected on warmup grounds); duration facts (the frozen adapter normalizes instant facts only); any OHLCV-derived fundamental proxy (forbidden); FRED/ALFRED, FINRA, Alpha Vantage, ECB, BIS (BLOCKED/out-of-scope, fail closed).
pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.availability_semantics: SEC filed dates are date-only: availability is stamped at the END of the filed UTC day (conservative upper bound; retrieval time never substitutes). A record influences decisions no earlier than its availability stamp plus one session, implemented exactly by pit_conditioning.session_gate_utc: a row is usable for decision session S iff available_time_utc < 00:00 UTC of S. Re-filed values supersede strictly after their own availability (fusion select_asof), never retroactively. PIT regression pin: tests/assets/stocks/test_pit_conditioning_adoption.py mutates availability stamps and must observe invisibility of any row at or after the gate.
pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.aggregate_construction: M_i(t) = single-vintage equal-weight mean of us-gaap:Assets over the sector-i filers INCLUDED at t, computed by aggregate_sector_asof with sorted entity order and math.fsum. The aggregate is single-vintage by bridge semantics: one effective date per sector per call (the latest effective date at which at least one participating filer has a gated record), and exactly the filers holding a selected value at that effective date are included - M_i(t) is literally the average balance sheet of the panel members reporting the newest fiscal period end. SectorObservation.coverage = filers_included/filers_mapped is reported per observation.
pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.anchor_key: g_i(t) = ln(M_i(t) / M_i(t-252s)), where t-252s is the SPY session exactly 252 sessions before t on the frozen calendar (the year-ago seasonal vintage). Both endpoints are PIT panel values; no future session is ever read.
pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.eligibility_gates_frozen: (a) sector pre-S0 fundability per census >= 0.80 (all 11 sectors pass for us-gaap:Assets); (b) at every tick, the sector observation at BOTH t and t-252s must have coverage >= 0.60 (filing-season lead-in weeks can thin the newest-vintage cohort; a thin vintage is not a signal, it is unaggregated data - the gate makes it FLAT instead); (c) if the two endpoint effective dates of the key differ by more than 100 calendar days the sector is ineligible at that tick; (d) the ETF leg requires >= 63 sessions of authorized adjusted-close history through t (XLC's 2018-06-19 inception delays its first leg eligibility to ~2018-09; before that XLC is held FLAT - an availability rule, not a selection). An ineligible sector is FLAT at that tick; the cross-section is never emptied by construction (>= 9 sectors eligible at every tick under these gates).
pit_observable_with_availability_semanti.warmup: first S0 decision tick 2018-04-04 requires the gated reference aggregate at ~2017-04-05 (pre-S0) - exactly what the coverage census certifies (pre-S0 availability fractions above) - plus 252 sessions of pre-S0 price runway for the kappa_t beta regression, identical to V4 warmup practice. No scored computation reads any session after 2025-07-31.

aggregation_declaration.binding_rule: per d1_proposal_packet binding_rules.aggregation_declaration: the following are frozen ex ante at family freeze and are NEVER tuned after scored PnL is visible.
aggregation_declaration.max_filing_gap_days_rationale: 400 days (~13.3 months) exceeds the 12-month filing cycle: annual-only 10-K filers keep contributing between their annual stamps, quarterly filers trivially stay in, and a filer that stops filing (merger, delisting, failure) drops out of the participating set about one quarter after its last availability stamp. Survivorship is thus governed by the explicit PIT filing-clock rule of the bridge, never by silent panel trimming; the parameter is constant across all three arms of this family and across all V5 families of this agent.
aggregation_declaration.aggregation_statistic: single-vintage equal-weight mean over sorted filers (math.fsum), exactly as returned by aggregate_sector_asof; no winsorizing, no size weighting, no vintage blending.
aggregation_declaration.key_transform: g_i(t) = ln(M_i(t)/M_i(t-252s)); control key ln(M_i(t)); no smoothing, no rank averaging across ticks.

universe_warmup_clock_holding_fills.universe: frozen 12-ETF cohort (SPY + XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY). SPY is reserved as benchmark context per the frozen benchmark contract and is NEVER a held leg. Decisions are taken on sector ETFs; conditioning comes from the SEC filer panel per sector via the canonical bridge. Leg-eligibility of an ETF is an availability rule only: >= 63 sessions of authorized {SYM}_all adjusted-close history through the decision session (delays XLC to ~2018-09; all other cohort ETFs eligible from S0 start).
universe_warmup_clock_holding_fills.warmup_sessions: 252-session PIT aggregate history (pre-S0, census-certified) + 252-session pre-S0 price runway for the beta regression; first decision tick 2018-04-04 is already valid.
universe_warmup_clock_holding_fills.decision_clock: quarterly session-count clock: every 63rd SPY session (252/4), RE-SEEDED at the first session of each frozen fold (S0_FOLD_1 2018-04-04..2020-09-01, S0_FOLD_2 2020-09-10..2023-02-09, S0_FOLD_3 2023-02-17..2025-07-24 per baseline_invariants.json). Ticks at fold-session offsets 0, 63, ..., 567: 10 ticks per fold (each fold has >= 599 sessions >= the 568 required), 30 scored decision periods total. Signals are computed at the tick on session-t PIT data only; force-flat and automaton re-seed at every fold boundary.
universe_warmup_clock_holding_fills.holding_period: 63 sessions (one clock period); weights static between ticks; the book opened at offset 567 is force-flattened at the fold boundary (truncated hold is a scored decision per the frozen convention).
universe_warmup_clock_holding_fills.fill_clock: next allowed session after the decision close, open-adjacent close-to-close execution per baseline invariants (V3 ADJ-1-EXEC-CLOCK); no same-session fill ever.

anchor_neighbour_causal_negative_control.anchor: SFV5-A4-H1-ANCHOR (BSFLOW-YOY-L3S3-63), exact rule, no parameter menu: (1) build M_i(t) for all 11 sectors from the us-gaap:Assets PIT panel per the frozen aggregation declaration; compute g_i(t) = ln(M_i(t)/M_i(t-252s)); apply the frozen eligibility gates. (2) Rank eligible sectors by g DESCENDING (rank 1 = fastest expansion, rank N = most contracted); ties broken lexicographically by symbol. (3) Hysteresis book automaton (same deterministic shape as the V4 SFV4-A4-H1 anchor, K = 3): seed at each fold's first tick - LONG := ranks N-2..N (the 3 most contracted), SHORT := ranks 1..3 (the 3 fastest expanding); subsequent ticks, applied in fixed order: (i) exits - a LONG whose new rank <= N-K-1 = N-4 leaves LONG (to SHORT if its new rank <= K = 3 and |SHORT| < 3, else FLAT); a SHORT whose new rank >= K+2 = 5 leaves SHORT (to LONG if its new rank >= N-2 and |LONG| < 3, else FLAT); (ii) entries - FLAT sectors with rank >= N-2 enter LONG in ascending-growth order while |LONG| < 3; FLAT sectors with rank <= 3 enter SHORT in descending-growth order while |SHORT| < 3; ties lexicographic. (4) Weights: +1/6 per LONG leg, -1/6 per SHORT leg (weights +/-1/(2K) if K ever degenerates below 3 under the frozen floor rule K = min(3, floor(N/3)), N = eligible count >= 9 here); CASH absorbs residual; gross <= 1.0, net ~ 0; long/short books accounted separately per baseline invariants; weights static between ticks. This is the single primary arm; the 3+3 baskets, band <= K+1 / > N-K-1, 252-session differencing, 63-session clock and 1/6 weights are fixed ex ante with no alternatives offered.
anchor_neighbour_causal_negative_control.neighbour: SFV5-A4-H1-NEIGH (BSFLOW-2Q-L3S3-63), one fixed variant supporting the same mechanism: identical to the anchor in every element (eligibility gates, 3+3 hysteresis automaton, weights, clock, holding, fills, costs, accounting) except the differencing span is 126 sessions (two filing quarters) instead of 252: g2_i(t) = ln(M_i(t)/M_i(t-126s)). Mechanism-support logic: if the premium attaches to balance-sheet expansion VELOCITY as such, the faster-sampled velocity carries the same sign with noisier ranks; agreement of the two spans supports the mechanism while disagreement marks the 252-session anchor as window-specific. No other variant is proposed.

causal_negative_control.control: SFV5-A4-H1-CTRL (BSLEVEL-L3S3-63): identical surface form to the anchor - same eligibility gates, same N, same rank-and-hysteresis 3+3 book at +/-1/6, same 63-session clock with per-fold reseed, same holding, same fills, same costs, same risk-match and neutralization - but the ranking key is the LOG LEVEL of the aggregate, ln(M_i(t)): LONG the 3 smallest aggregate balance sheets, SHORT the 3 largest. The anchor key is the first difference of the control key: the control is not a different variable, it is the orthogonal transformation of the SAME variable, which is what makes the identification causal rather than cosmetic.
causal_negative_control.why_cannot_reproduce_mechanism: The preregistered mechanism (Zhang q-theory; Cooper-Gulen-Schill; Titman-Wei-Xie) is a statement about the RATE of change of the asset base - investment flow - not about cross-sector balance-sheet scale. rank(DELTA ln M) is not a function of rank(ln M): two filer panels with identical level orderings but different growth orderings produce byte-identical control books and opposite anchor books. A sector can hold the largest balance sheet and any growth rank at once. Under its preregistered rule the control can carry only an aggregate-size bet, for which no documented premium exists in this universe after market/sector neutralization; if it nevertheless reproduces the anchor's spread, the claimed investment-flow mechanism is falsified and the spread belongs to a scale axis.
causal_negative_control.why_not_the_L7_trap: L7 (V4): controls died pre-selection at measured control self-subsumption rho 0.78-0.83 because stale ranks of persistent states are rank-identical to their anchors. A one-tick-stale or four-tick-stale asset-GROWTH control is exactly that trap - growth ranks are highly persistent - and is PROHIBITED as this family's control. The level control is the differencing-inverse of the anchor, not a lagged copy: lag correlation of the flow is near one by persistence, while stock-vs-flow rank correlation is structurally unconstrained and empirically low across sectors whose scale structure (order-of-magnitude mean-asset differences between filer panels) dominates level ranks while growth ranks order expansion phase.
causal_negative_control.control_can_fire: The control is a live rule, not a stub: ln(M_i) has strictly positive cross-sectional dispersion at every tick and fills 3+3 baskets at every tick (N >= 9); it trades through the same hysteresis automaton and incurs the same costs. A control that cannot fire identifies nothing; this one can.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: The anchor passes only if |control risk-matched incremental alpha| < 0.5 x |anchor risk-matched incremental alpha| (frozen gate control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt = 0.5) AND control expectancy <= 0. If the control's expectancy > 0 with PF >= 1.0, or the ratio reaches 0.5, the spread is attributed to the balance-sheet LEVEL axis, the family is REJECTED, and no alternate control may be substituted after results are seen.

anchor_neighbour_causal_negative_control.control_identifiability_verification_for: A9-F verifies identifiability from frozen inputs alone (PIT store sha f53eb371..., panel.json, frozen SPY calendar) by recomputing, WITHOUT any PnL or trading: (1) the anchor key and control key for all 11 sectors at all 30 ticks; (2) Spearman rank correlation between anchor and control keys across eligible sectors at each tick - preregistered identifiability gate: mean |rho| over the 30 ticks <= 0.40 AND max |rho| <= 0.60 (V4 died at 0.78-0.83; a family above these bounds is control-subsumed and INELIGIBLE pre-selection); (3) CAN-FIRE: control cross-sectional dispersion > 0 at every tick AND at least 5 basket-membership changes of the control book across the 30 ticks (a control whose book never changes identifies nothing); (4) coverage-gate non-emptiness: >= 9 rank-eligible sectors at every tick. All four checks are deterministic rank arithmetic on declared PIT panels and are reproducible from the store hash in seconds.

incremental_alpha_test.risk_matched_incremental_alpha: Mandatory primary test per baseline invariants: incremental_alpha(arm, window) = R_arm(window) - R_spy_context(window), with R_spy_context = SPY total return (adjusted _all path, frozen benchmark contract) scaled EX ANTE by this arm's frozen rule, never realized gross re-applied after the fact. Frozen scaling rule (net ~ 0 book): kappa_t = clip(beta_hat_t, 0.0, 2.0), where beta_hat_t is the OLS slope of the arm's own daily book returns (a deterministic function of the frozen rule, hence PIT-computable at t) on SPY total-return daily returns over the trailing 252 sessions ending t-1; if fewer than 63 sessions of arm history exist at a tick, kappa_t := 0. Evaluated per fold AND overall; gates: anchor overall alpha > 0, risk-matched excess positive in >= 2/3 folds (frozen stage-A).
incremental_alpha_test.sector_factor_neutralization: All legs are sector ETFs, so the optional equal-weight sector factor (EW_SECTOR total return per the frozen benchmark contract) is used as a required secondary diagnostic: OLS of the arm's daily returns on [SPY total return, EW_SECTOR total return] per fold and overall; the annualized intercepts are reported alongside the primary metric. A result whose residual intercept after both-factor removal is not positive fails the mechanism claim regardless of raw PnL.
incremental_alpha_test.fail_closed: raw PnL, gross beta or long-equity exposure is never accepted as alpha (L6); every gate above fails closed per baseline invariants; a control that outperforms a negative anchor falsifies the family.

base_and_stress_costs.cost_model: 10 bps per side per fill at base; 20 bps per side per fill at stress; charged exactly once per fill (P1-A2 invariant 2, L2); benchmark paths uncosted per contract.
base_and_stress_costs.expected_base_drag: at the expected ~1.1-2.4 two-way turnover per year (point estimate ~1.8), base drag is ~11-24 bps/year (point ~18 bps); at stress ~22-48 bps/year (point ~36 bps). The quarterly filing cadence of the underlying signal (the aggregate updates ~4 vintages per year) is the structural reason the arm can afford to be slow.
base_and_stress_costs.stress_rerun: full value-book rerun at 20 bps/side is part of the family's scored evidence; frozen gates: stress PnL > 0 and stress PF >= 1.0.

turnover_and_sample_floor.convention: turnover = sum(abs(delta_weight)) over non-CASH legs (frozen ADJ-5 convention, L3), reported annualized two-way, both raw and ceiling-normalized.
turnover_and_sample_floor.expected_turnover: 63-session quarterly clock: ~4.06 ticks/year. Growth ranks of balance-sheet aggregates are persistent and move only at filing vintages, so with hysteresis bands of width 1 the expected churn is 0.5-1.5 leg swaps per tick, each swap moving 2 x 1/6 = 1/3 of |delta w|: ~0.7-2.0 per year from rebalances, plus 3 force-flat boundary events over the 7.3-year S0 (1.0 each) ~ +0.41/year: expected ~1.1-2.4, point estimate ~1.8 two-way per year - 30% of the frozen 6.0 ceiling.
turnover_and_sample_floor.why_inside_ceiling: the design spends turnover only on genuine state transitions of a quarterly fundamental statistic; hysteresis + persistence of annual-vintage aggregates + static weights between ticks structurally cap churn far below the ceiling with headroom for stress and boundary flattening. The honest worst case (full 3+3 reconstitution at every tick, ~8.0/year) breaches the ceiling BY DESIGN and would itself evidence that aggregate growth ranks carry no stable ordering - accepted as part of the falsification structure rather than loosened by a turncoat schedule.
turnover_and_sample_floor.sample_floor: 10 scored decision periods per fold x 3 folds = 30 per arm - the frozen floor (>= 30 total, >= 5 per fold) is met EXACTLY with ~6% session margin per fold (each fold needs >= 568 sessions for 10 ticks; folds have >= 599). Zero-margin honesty: if any tick were lost to degeneracy the arm fails the floor by arithmetic and dies in feasibility; no clock loosening is permitted. Positions: >= 6 non-CASH legs at every tick (never fewer than 4 under the K = min(3, floor(N/3)) rule with N >= 9), satisfying the min-positions invariant.

drop_one_design.expected_max_concentration: 6 equal legs at 1/6 of gross each; ex ante no sector should dominate spread contributions. The honest hazard is a persistent single-sector relation - e.g., one sector's contraction episode (2020 demand collapse or the 2023-2025 AI-capex expansion divergence in XLK) dominating fold contributions and pushing one ETF's positive-PnL share above the frozen etf_positive_share_le = 0.35 gate; this is treated as a live hazard, not assumed away.
drop_one_design.drop_one_etf: full value-book rerun excluding the max-contribution symbol (frozen convention; the cross-section shrinks by one, baskets and automaton unchanged); survival = after-drop expectancy > 0. Meaningful because the claim is a cross-sectional aggregate premium - it must not be one sector's episode.
drop_one_design.drop_one_fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed; survival = min > 0. Meaningful because the three folds span structurally distinct fundamental regimes - fold 1 holds the 2018 rate shock, the 2019 late-cycle investment peak and the COVID contraction; fold 2 the reopening/reflation capex boom and supply-chain asset expansion; fold 3 the AI-capex concentration expansion - and a genuine expansion-velocity premium must not be a single-regime artifact.
drop_one_design.caveat_declared_ex_ante: fold 1 carries the COVID episode; if the entire anchor expectancy is the 2020 contraction, drop-one-fold fails by construction and the family is rejected - no fold re-weighting or exclusion is permitted.

failure_interpretation: A Stage-A reject means the expansion velocity of sector filer panels carries no exploitable after-cost, market-neutral information at sector-ETF granularity: the single-name asset-growth anomaly (Cooper-Gulen-Schill; Titman-Wei-Xie; Zhang's q-theory investment channel) does not transmit to 11 large liquid sector composites, is absorbed by the balance-sheet LEVEL axis (control fires), or is SPY/sector-factor exposure (neutralization gate). Sharper sub-cases: anchor negative with control negative = no signal, the flow axis is inert; anchor negative with control positive = raw PnL on this cohort is the scale/exposure form, not the mechanism (the exact V4 failure mode); anchor positive with control positive at ratio >= 0.5 = level subsumption, mechanism falsified. Every outcome is terminal for this family in V5 - no window, span, basket, gate or clock tweak may be proposed to rescue it - and the verdict counts once in the historical denominator. A correct reject is a successful research run.
source_to_test_map: 1. Zhang (2005) q-theory + Cooper-Gulen-Schill (2008) + Titman-Wei-Xie (2004) -> joint implication: high investment/balance-sheet growth predicts LOW forward returns -> implemented as the anchor key g_i(t) = ln(M_i(t)/M_i(t-252s)) built from the us-gaap:Assets PIT panel; feature goldens hand-computed in tests/assets/stocks/test_sec_aggregate_features.py against research/assets/stocks/sec_aggregate_features.py (to be written in the I phase from this frozen specification).

2. PIT availability semantics (filed-date end-of-UTC-day stamps + conditioning-lag rule) -> research/assets/stocks/pit_conditioning.py session_gate_utc/usable_for_session/conditioning_panel with max_filing_gap_days = 400; regression-pinned by tests/assets/stocks/test_pit_conditioning_adoption.py (existing) + family mutation tests in tests/assets/stocks/test_v5_family_bshexpansion.py (any record with a later availability stamp must be invisible; stale-vintage read must fail).

3. Single-vintage aggregation, coverage reporting, survivorship via the filing-clock rule -> bridge aggregate_sector_asof + SectorObservation.coverage; frozen eligibility gates (census floor 0.80; coverage >= 0.60 at both endpoints; 100-day effective-date coherence) pinned in tests/assets/stocks/test_v5_family_bshexpansion.py with fixture filers that stop filing.

4. Mechanism must not be beta -> net ~ 0 book, frozen kappa_t = clip(trailing-252 OLS beta, 0, 2) risk-matched SPY-context subtraction and [SPY, EW_SECTOR] intercept neutralization -> research/assets/stocks/factory.py + family arm module; mirrors the V4 factor-alpha suite in tests/assets/stocks/.

5. Mechanism must be flow, not level -> preregistered BSLEVEL-L3S3-63 control with the 0.5 alpha-ratio + expectancy <= 0 falsification rule; control-cannot-equal-anchor pinned as a deterministic rank-arithmetic regression (control key != anchor key at every tick; mean |Spearman| <= 0.40, max <= 0.60 measured on the frozen panels) in tests/assets/stocks/test_v5_family_bshexpansion.py - the L7 lesson made into a test.
6. Mechanism robustness across sampling of the same flow -> 126-session-span neighbour must carry the same sign -> neighbour arm in the same family module.

7. Survival after costs and bounds -> frozen 10/20 bps schedules (research/assets/stocks/execution.py, accounting invariants in research/assets/stocks/accounting.py), ADJ-5 turnover ceiling 6.0, force-flat fold boundaries, next-session fills (research/assets/stocks/calendar.py/execution.py) -> existing P1 suites + family integration tests.

8. Cross-sectional robustness -> drop-one ETF and drop-one fold reruns per baseline invariants -> value_book rerun harness, non-vacuity asserted (the dropped symbol must change the book) in tests/assets/stocks/test_v5_family_bshexpansion.py.
forbidden_inventory_screen: Checked against every entry of forbidden_family_inventory.json and PLAN_stocks_v5.md Section 1: (1) A4_XSEC_ETF_RELATIVE_MOMENTUM - NOT touched: the ranking key is a SEC-filed aggregate of total assets; it contains no price, no return and no relative-strength term, and the long side is the CONTRACTING side (anti-momentum in price space is not claimed or implied). (2) A5-SFV2-TREND-DEFENSIVE - no SMA/EMA/trend/vol-target element; gross is a frozen constant, exposure is never scaled by volatility or drawdown. (3) SFV3-A5-IDIO-SHOCK-REVERSAL - no idiosyncratic shock, no residual-return term, no event-conditioned countertrade; the book holds a persistent fundamental state, it does not fade shocks. (4) SFV3-A6-TOM-SETTLE - no calendar-date seasonality; the 63-session clock is a session-count grid on the SPY calendar with per-fold reseed, and no return claim attaches to calendar dates. (5) SFV4-A5-H1-PARTICIPATION-SHIFT and its inversion - no dollar-volume, no fresh/stale volume ratio, no participation term of any kind. (6) SFV4-A4-H1-SEMIVARIANCE-SHARE and vol-level inversion - no squared-return, no semivariance, no volatility quantity anywhere in the key; this family is NOT the Section 1.1 vol-level re-entry (reserved for another agent) and claims no relationship to it. (7) EQ_S2_A3_F1_PIT_RECON_FLOW - that entry is a paid-sprint market-data PIT reconstruction/flow family (never scored); this proposal reconstructs no market data and its 'flow' is the real-investment flow of SEC-reported assets - different object, different data lane. (8) A5-S2-F1-LENDING-CONSTRAINT-PREMIUM - no securities-lending data. Generic list: no cross-sectional momentum, no standalone trend/defensive rotation, no beta-dressed result (incremental alpha mandatory), no earnings-surprise/analyst/flows/borrow/spread mechanism, no daily-indicator grid, no new accounts/paid data/network fetch. Relaxed-gate rescue (Section 1 item 7): none - this is a new PIT-conditioned mechanism with all Stage-A gates unrelaxed.

implementation_estimate.engineer_days: ~3 days: feature module from the frozen spec (0.5), anchor/neighbour/control arm configs sharing one book engine (1.0), control-identifiability + PIT mutation + control-cannot-equal-anchor tests (0.75), drop-one/stress/turnover harness wiring (0.5), fold force-flat + reseed integration (0.25)
implementation_estimate.risk_notes: (1) panel-composition drift: filers joining the mean mid-S0 shift the aggregate level at their join anniversary; bounded by the census fractions (<= 20% of any sector's panel joins over the whole pre-S0 window) and declared as accepted noise, constant across arms - it is a reason the anchor may be noisy, not a post-hoc excuse. (2) filing-season lead-in: the 0.60 vintage-coverage gate makes thin-cohort ticks FLAT instead of inventing a signal; eligibility flicker adds bounded, declared churn. (3) XLC leg delay to ~2018-09 is an availability rule; conditioning for XLC filers is independent and unaffected. (4) kappa_t regression must use arm history through t-1 only (no leakage); pinned by mutation test.
